# Unquoted YAML scalar with colon-space breaks parsing

**Date**: 2026-05-29
**Category**: wrong-assumption

## What Happened

While authoring claude-kit's `references/index.yaml` (PR159), a reference description was written as
an unquoted scalar containing a colon-space:

```yaml
references:
  - path: rules.md
    description: How to author a rule. ... use-case-oriented paths: design, consolidation/...
```

The `paths: ` (colon followed by a space) inside the unquoted `description` value is interpreted by
YAML as the start of a **nested mapping key**, not literal text. `yaml.safe_load` then failed with
`mapping values are not allowed here`. Because `inject_references.py` parses `index.yaml` with
`yaml.safe_load`, a broken index would silently disable injection for that plugin.

The same hazard exists in `injection_rules.yaml` and any other YAML file with free-text values.

## How to Avoid

- When writing a free-text value in YAML (descriptions, summaries), **never put `word: ` (colon +
  space) inside an unquoted scalar**. Rephrase to drop the colon-space (`paths: design` →
  `path-pattern design`), or wrap the whole value in quotes (`description: "… paths: design …"`).
- After editing any `index.yaml` / `index.jp.yaml` / `injection_rules.yaml`, validate it:
  `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))" <file>` — and run the
  index↔injection_rules↔filesystem orphan check.
- Note: a colon **without** a trailing space (e.g. `a:b`) does not trigger this; it is specifically
  `: ` (colon-space) and ` #` that YAML treats specially in plain scalars.

## Context

- Affects: `plugins/*-kit/references/index.yaml` (+ `index.jp.yaml`), `injection_rules.yaml`, and any
  YAML consumed by `inject_references.py`.
- Discovered in PR159 (claude-kit → ref-inject migration) when the orphan-check script first failed
  to even parse `index.yaml`.
